flags: IHS Holding Limited entered into a definitive merger agreement with MTN Group Limited to be acquired for $8.50 per share in cash, subject to closing conditions including shareholder approval (two-thirds vote), regulatory approvals, and maintenance of specified cash levels; the shares will be delisted from the NYSE upon completion.

IHS completed the sale of its entire Latin American tower operations (Brazil and Colombia) to Macquarie Asset Management for an enterprise value of approximately $952 million, announced on February 17, 2026 and completed in August 2026.
IHS completed the sale of its 51.0% stake in I-Systems (its Brazilian FTTH fiber business) to TIM S.A., announced on February 11, 2026 and completed in May 2026.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in P1 (20-F Item 4, Business Overview).
business_model.claim: IHS Towers is an independent owner, operator and developer of shared communications infrastructure (cellular towers) that provides coverage and connectivity to approximately 647 million people in emerging markets across two regions and seven countries.
quotes: We are one of the largest independent owners, operators and developers of shared communications infrastructure in the world, providing our customers, most of whom are leading MNOs, with critical infrastructure that facilitates mobile communications coverage and connectivity for approximately 647 million people in emerging markets, across two regions and seven countries.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in P1 (20-F Item 4, Business Overview).
business_model.claim: The company's core revenue-generating services are Colocation (adding tenants to existing towers), Lease Amendments (adding equipment or ancillary services), New Site construction, Fiber-to-the-Tower in Nigeria, and in-building/DAS solutions.
quotes: We provide our customers with opportunities to lease space on existing Towers alongside current Tenants, known as Colocation, to install additional equipment on a Tower or request certain ancillary services, known as Lease Amendments, or to commission the construction of new Towers to the customer's specifications, known as New Sites.

business_model.claim: As of December 31, 2025, IHS operated 37,590 towers supporting 54,874 tenants at a Colocation Rate of 1.46x across five African and two Latin American countries.
quotes: As of December 31, 2025, we operated 37,590 Towers across five countries in Africa and two countries in Latin America.
As of December 31, 2025, our owned and operated tower portfolio supported 54,874 Tenants, with a Colocation Rate of 1.46x.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in P2 (20-F Risk Factors).
business_model.claim: Customers are predominantly leading Mobile Network Operators (MNOs); the top three MNO customers in each individual market collectively accounted for 99% of consolidated revenue in both 2025 and 2024.
quotes: revenue from our top three MNO customers, considered in each of our individual markets of operation, collectively accounted for 99% and 99%, respectively, of our consolidated revenue.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in P3 (20-F Item 5) and P5 (Q3 2026 6-K MD&A).
business_model.claim: The company reports three operating segments: Nigeria, Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA; Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire, South Africa, Zambia, and until October 2025 Rwanda), and Latin America (Latam; Brazil and Colombia), with Latam reclassified as a discontinued operation after disposals completed in May and August 2026.
quotes: Our three operating segments are Nigeria, which comprises our operations in Nigeria; Sub Saharan Africa, or SSA, which comprises our operations in Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire, South Africa, Zambia (and, until October 9, 2025, Rwanda); and Latin America, or Latam, which comprises our operations in Brazil and Colombia.
In May 2026 and August 2026, the Group completed the I-Systems Disposal and the Latam Towers Disposal respectively.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in P3 (20-F Item 5, Our Revenue).
business_model.claim: Revenue is decomposed into organic (colocation, lease amendments, contractual escalators, power indexation, FX resets, new site construction, fiber, churn), inorganic (acquisitions and disposals), and non-core (FX translation) components.
quotes: Organic revenue captures the performance of our existing business without the impact of new tower portfolios or businesses acquired since the beginning of the prior year period (except as described as inorganic below). Specifically, organic revenue captures the impact of (i) new Colocation and Lease Amendments; (ii) changes in pricing including from contractual lease fee escalation, power indexation and foreign exchange resets; (iii) New Site construction; (iv) fiber connectivity and (v) any impact of Churn and decommissioning.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in P1 (20-F Item 4, Business Overview).
business_model.claim: MLAs are typically 5 to 10 years in duration with annual or semi-annual inflation-linked revenue escalators; Key Customers (93% of tenants) had aggregate Contracted Revenue of $11.1 billion and an average remaining lease term of 7.5 years as of December 31, 2025.
quotes: we typically enter into long-term MLAs of 5 to 10 years in duration

As of December 31, 2025, the average remaining length of our MLAs with our Key Customers, who represented 93% of our Tenants, was 6.4 years. Additionally, these Key Customers had aggregate Contracted Revenue of $11.1 billion and an average remaining lease term of 7.5 years.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in P1 (20-F Item 4, Business Overview).

quotes: For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, 47%, 52% and 55%, respectively, of our revenue from continuing operations was linked to the U.S. dollar and euro.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in P5 (Q3 2026 6-K MD&A) and P6 (Q3 2026 earnings release).
business_model.claim: The principal cost driver is power generation (diesel and electricity), as evidenced by a year-on-year increase in power generation costs of $38.8 million in Q3 2026 attributed to higher global power prices including the Middle East conflict.
quotes: During the third quarter the increase in costs was primarily driven by a year-on-year increase in power generation costs ($38.8 million), as a result of higher global power prices due to reasons including the conflict in the Middle East.

Higher cost of sales was primarily attributable to higher power generation costs in the Nigeria segment, driven by increased diesel prices associated with reasons including the conflict in the Middle East.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in P3 (20-F Item 5, Factors Affecting Our Financial Condition).
business_model.claim: Incremental capital expenditure for Colocation or Lease Amendments is typically $5,000–$10,000 per site in African markets, while building a new tower site costs $50,000–$100,000 in Africa and $40,000–$80,000 in Latin America.
quotes: Typically, the main incremental cost to deliver Colocation or Lease Amendments is between $5,000 and $10,000 in augmentation capital expenditure, and from $10,000 to $12,000 in our Latin America business.

The average cost to build a New Site in our African markets is typically in the range of between $50,000 and $100,000, while in Latin America the cost is typically in the range of between $40,000 and $80,000 depending on the market of operation and specification of the tower.

quotes: From June 14, 2023 to March 31, 2024, the NFEM rate depreciated by 64.4%, from approximately ₦474.0 to $1.00 to approximately ₦1,330.8 to $1.00, while the Bloomberg rate depreciated by 66.1%, from approximately ₦472.3 to $1.00 to approximately ₦1,393.5 to $1.00 during the same period.
For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, 47%, 52% and 55%, respectively, of our revenue from continuing operations was linked to the U.S. dollar and euro.

While the exchange rate was less volatile in 2025, with the Naira appreciating 6.7% against the U.S. dollar during the year, there can be no assurance that it will not further depreciate in the future.
